extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners / IP attorneys drafting or prosecuting U.S. patent claims (particularly biotech/antibody matters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards on (1) the Jepson claim format and (2) how written description and means-plus-function rules apply to Jepson-format and functionally‑defined claims, illustrated by the In re Xencor decision and USPTO/MPEP positions. Focused on U.S. patent prosecution and litigation for biotech/antibody inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jepson claim format (37 CFR § 1.75(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Jepson claim has a specific format: (1) a preamble comprising a general description of all the elements or steps of the claimed combination which are conventional or known, (2) a phrase such as 'wherein the improvement comprises,' and (3) those elements, steps and/or relationships which constitute that portion of the claimed combination which the applicant considers as the new or improved portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the three-part structure: (i) preamble identifying conventional/known features, (ii) specific transitional phrase indicating the improvement, and (iii) recitation of the new or improved aspects. (Verbatim text from 37 CFR § 1.75(e) as cited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement applies to the entire Jepson claim (including the preamble)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Jepson claim preamble requires written description; the inventor must provide written description sufficient for the claim's totality, which necessarily includes the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Circuit: 'The invention [of a Jepson claim] is not only the claimed improvement, but the claimed improvement as applied to the prior art, so the inventor must provide written description sufficient to show possession of the claimed improvement to what was known in the prior art.' Also: 'While a Jepson claim is directed to the improvement it makes to the prior art, the claim is a singular thing and cannot be separated; its totality is what must have written description support...' — thus do not assume the preamble can escape §112 analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor must show possession of the claimed improvement as applied to the prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession must be shown not just of the improvement in the abstract but of the improvement as applied to what was known in the prior art; you cannot avoid written description by asserting portions are 'well-known.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court admonition: 'A patentee cannot be permitted to use a Jepson claim to avoid the requirement that she be in possession of the claimed invention simply by asserting something is well-known in the art.' If relying on assertedly known prior-art features, provide specification support or evidence that those features were indeed well-known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description sufficiency for a claimed genus (antibodies) — need species disclosure or proof of well-known genus
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming a genus of antibodies (various specificities/epitopes), disclosing only a single antibody species may be insufficient to satisfy the written description requirement for the broader genus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Xencor the specification disclosed only one anti-C5 antibody (5G1.1), which the USPTO found insufficient given the 'various specificities and epitopes' of the genus. To support a genus claim, disclose representative species or otherwise show that the genus was known/would be understood by an ordinary artisan to be within the inventor's possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function claiming under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: An element may be expressed as a means or step for performing a specified function without reciting structure, material, or acts; such a claim is construed to cover the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification and equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory text (35 U.S.C. § 112(f)) and MPEP § 2181 govern interpretation: during examination the means-plus-function clause is interpreted as reciting 'the structure, material or act described in the specification as performing the entire claimed function and equivalents.' Ensure the specification discloses corresponding structure (e.g., the actual antibody species) if using means-plus-function language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional claiming / genus support under Ariad (species sufficiency requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims use functional language to define the boundaries of a claimed genus, the specification must show that the inventor has invented species sufficient to support a claim to the functionally‑defined genus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing Ariad (en banc), MPEP § 2181 notes that functional/genus claims require adequate species disclosure. Courts may require multiple representative species or other disclosure demonstrating reduction to practice across the claimed scope; otherwise the claim risks failing written description even if framed functionally or as means-plus-function.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO practice: examiners treat Jepson preambles as part of the invention and may invalidate claims for lack of written description
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's position is that Jepson claim preambles are part of the invention and thus require written description; the USPTO in Xencor invalidated claims for lack of written description in the preamble ('method of treating' clause).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to defend Jepson-format claims on the merits (specification support for preamble and improvement) rather than relying solely on formal claim labeling; appeals may fail if specification lacks species or other support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical caution on 'clever' claim drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: While judges criticize attempts to use clever claim drafting to avoid statutory requirements, practitioners often try different drafting approaches because claim scope can hinge on precise wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a particular claim label (Jepson, means-plus-function) will circumvent written description or other statutory requirements; draft with sufficient specification support for the claimed scope. As Judge Rich noted: 'the name of the game is the claims.'
